name: Conoclinium

project_scope.taxonomy_note: Conoclinium greggii is treated as a synonym of Conoclinium dissectum by POWO and Flora of North America.
project_scope.scope_note: Both species are installed in data/manifest.json; this corrects the earlier genus file that listed only dissectum.

study_strategy.warning: Many horticultural and older Texas sources still use the name Conoclinium greggii.

look_here_first: Separate these two from a single fully expanded middle stem leaf: C. dissectum has a blade cut into obvious lobes/dissections; C. coelestinum has an intact triangular/ovate outline with marginal teeth but no deep lobes. Confirm opposite leaves and blue-violet rayless heads. Do not identify from flower color alone.
shared_genus_traits: Usually rhizomatous perennial with opposite leaves, often 3 main veins from the base
Small blue/lavender to violet heads composed only of disk florets; clustered in terminal/axillary corymbiform arrays
Approximately 25 phyllaries in 2–3 series around hemispheric involucres; cone-shaped receptacle without paleae
Persistent pappus bristles on five-ribbed cypselae

species_comparison_matrix.conoclinium_dissectum: Deeply lobed/dissected blade, often giving a palmleaf outline
species_comparison_matrix.conoclinium_coelestinum: Undissected triangular/deltate/ovate blade with serrate/dentate/crenate teeth
species_comparison_matrix.priority: PRIMARY field discriminator; check mature leaves from several nodes
Microscopic corroboration; flower-head photo should include scale
High-value reproductive confirmation when mature fruit is available

species_comparison_matrix.conoclinium_dissectum: Rhizomatous, many stems, sometimes knotty crown or somewhat woody at base
species_comparison_matrix.conoclinium_coelestinum: Colonial rhizomatous plant, usually erect, sometimes rooting at nodes

quick_comparison_steps: 1. Verify opposite leaves and terminal clusters of true Asteraceae capitula lacking rays.
2. Photograph a fully expanded middle stem leaf flat, including outline, petiole, and venation.
3. Deep lobes or dissections → C. dissectum; simple triangular/deltate blade with teeth → C. coelestinum.
4. When leaves are atypical or partly damaged, corroborate mature cypsela surface and length (hairy 1.8–2.5 mm versus smooth 1–1.5 mm), with scale.

local_lookalikes.learner_role: Canonical LOOKALIKE_COMPARISON; target zone native status UNRESOLVED; not native-counted
local_lookalikes.separate_by: Typically 8–10 mm long CYLINDRICAL involucre with 4–6 or more phyllary series vs much shorter Conoclinium heads with hemispheric involucres and only 2–3 phyllary series; often tall sprawling subshrub.
Woody evergreen shrub with white or faintly pink heads, and 4–6 mm involucres; verify stems and head structure, not color alone.
Herbaceous erect rhizomatous perennial with long-petioled coarsely toothed leaves and white heads.
Usually oblong/oblong-lanceolate leaves with truncate to cordate/subauriculate bases and dilated pappus bristle tips; regional occurrence must be checked before treating as local.

local_lookalikes.learner_role: Source-pool taxon (five personal iNaturalist wild observations); research-drafts/fleischmannia-incarnata.json; not yet canonical
local_lookalikes.separate_by: Opposite triangular leaves and pinkish rayless heads may look like C. coelestinum, but Fleischmannia generally has a lax/sprawling habit, about 13–25 disk florets per head (vs Conoclinium 35–70+) and a flat or nearly flat receptacle (vs conic). Flower color only supporting.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Side-by-side fully expanded leaves from both species, adaxial and abaxial, same scale
diagnostic_photo_checklist.label: dissected blade vs intact toothed blade; petiole; 3 basal veins

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Same-scale fruit/seed macros from both species
diagnostic_photo_checklist.label: C. dissectum hispidulous 1.8–2.5 mm vs C. coelestinum glabrous 1–1.5 mm

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Flower-head side macros with phyllaries and mm scale
diagnostic_photo_checklist.label: involucre, phyllaries, disk florets; do not mistake clusters for single heads

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Habit and habitat photos showing ground-level stems
diagnostic_photo_checklist.label: knotty crown/spreading versus rhizomatous colonies; supporting only
diagnostic_photo_checklist.status: existing broad views; fine diagnostic pair pending

taxonomic_safeguards: Conoclinium greggii and Eupatorium greggii are synonyms of accepted C. dissectum, not separate species pages.
Do not treat leaf color, bloom timing or head color alone as species separators.

arrows.label: deep lobe sinus
arrows.anchor: innermost clearly visible cleft between lobes

annotation_blueprint.warning: Do not point to a marginal tooth as if it were a lobe.

arrows.label: continuous margin
arrows.anchor: unbroken outer leaf outline between teeth

annotation_blueprint.warning: Do not circle a damaged or folded leaf and call it dissected.

arrows.label: involucre
arrows.anchor: phyllary basket directly below disk florets

annotation_blueprint.warning: Label a single capitulum, not the entire inflorescence as an involucre.
Include millimeter scale before asserting measured difference.

measurement_conflicts.resolution: Unreconciled variation across treatments. Avoid using length as a standalone hard cutoff. Use leaves and fruit hairiness; add paired voucher microscopy before a locked size key.

field_ready_image_pair.primary_teaching_point: Use LEAF BLADE OUTLINE—not flower color—to split Gregg's and blue mistflower.

paired_panels.teaching_annotation: Look for the blade divided deeply into prominent lobes
paired_panels.view_limit: Flowering/foliage context, not an isolated full leaf at scale

paired_panels.teaching_annotation: Look for opposite leaves whose continuous outline has teeth, not deep dissection
paired_panels.view_limit: Usable attached-leaf view, not an isolated leaf with ruler
